title: Old Norse Online, Lesson 10: Runes and Mystic Origins
author: Todd B. Krause and Jonathan Slocum
publisher: Linguistics Research Center, The University of Texas at Austin
notes: Scholarly reconstruction reference. The corpus uses the Older Futhark chart and preserves the authors' warning that later rune names should not be applied naively to early inscriptions.

title: Unicode NamesList: Runic (16A0–16FF)
author: Unicode Consortium
notes: Authoritative modern character identities and names; not evidence for ancient rune names.

title: Rune poems
notes: Revision 10795428 (2 January 2021), used as the fixed digital transcription witness for all 61 original-language stanza bodies. No English translations are bundled.

title: Linguarum veterum septentrionalium thesaurus grammatico-criticus et archæologicus
author: George Hickes
notes: Early printed witness preserving the Old English Rune Poem after the Cotton Otho B.x manuscript was damaged in the 1731 fire.

title: Runic and Heroic Poems of the Old Teutonic Peoples
author: Bruce Dickins
notes: Bibliography and locators only. Exact English translations are intentionally not bundled because worldwide redistribution status is not uniform; Dickins died in 1978.

title: Kylverstenen
notes: Object 267753_HST; runic signum G 88. Catalogue metadata dates the limestone object to 400–550 and identifies an Older Futhark inscription.

title: The Kylver Stone (G 88)
author: Tom Birkett
notes: Supporting record describing the complete older-futhark row; metadata/citation only, with no media redistributed.

title: RuneS: Runic Writing in the Germanic Languages
publisher: Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz
notes: Research database cited by stable inscription identities for the Vadstena and Grumpan bracteates and Charnay fibula.

title: Tacitus: Germania
author: Publius Cornelius Tacitus
publisher: Fordham University Internet History Sourcebooks Project
notes: Section 10 describes marked wooden lots; it does not identify Elder Futhark, runes, rune stones, a 24-piece bag, or modern spreads.

title: Inscribed sandstone fragments of Hole, Norway: radiocarbon dates provide insight into rune-stone traditions
author: Steinar Solheim et al.
notes: 2025 open-access archaeological study used only for contextual early-runic evidence, not as a complete rune-row witness.

title: Runes: A Handbook
author: Michael P. Barnes
notes: Modern scholarship bibliography; no copyrighted prose is reproduced.

title: The Book of Runes
author: Ralph Blum
notes: Modern oracle history only. No interpretation text is reproduced; the blank rune is not part of canonical Elder Futhark.

title: Das Geheimnis der Runen
author: Guido von List
notes: Later Armanen occult system, kept separate from Elder Futhark identity.
